title: Traffic Fail-safe Orchestra: policy-driven staged rollouts with emergency quench
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Deliver a modular policy engine and runtime orchestration layer for staged model rollouts that enforces traffic splits, step schedules, guardrails, and an emergency ‘quench’ auto-rollback. The goal is to provide product teams with a declarative DSL and runtime safeguards so deployments can ramp safely across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments with consistent enforcement and observability. This ticket covers the policy DSL extensions, runtime admission/enforcement hooks, simulation tooling, and integration points for Console and telemetry.
acceptance_criteria: Policy DSL supports: weighted traffic splits, step schedule timelines (duration and conditions), priority lanes (canary / control / shadow), and explicit guardrail predicates (error rate, latency p95, quality regressions)
Runtime enforcer evaluates policy at ingress and adjusts routing decisions with <= 50ms additional median latency under typical load
Automatic quench triggers on guardrail breach: pause ramp, scale back to previous stable variant, and surface actionable diagnostics in Console within 30s
Simulation harness can validate a policy against historical traffic traces and produce expected ramp curve + breach probability report
End-to-end tests (integration) for canonical scenarios: healthy rollout, transient spike (no rollback), sustained regression (auto-quench + rollback), and shadow-only validation
Console exposes per-step status, active guardrails, and a one-click rollback action for operators
design_notes: We will extend the existing rollout DSL (lightweight YAML/JSON) to include 'lanes' and 'quench' sections. Example: lanes: [{name: 'canary', weight: 5}, {name: 'control', weight: 95}, {name: 'shadow', mode: 'shadow'}]

Guardrails are expressed as predicates with short window aggregations (e.g., 5m error_rate > 2% AND latency_p95 > 1200ms). Each guardrail has a severity (warn|critical) and action (pause|quench|notify)
Routing uses hash-consistent sampling for deterministic user bucketing to lanes; sampling keys are configurable per route (user_id, session_id, request_id)

Quench (emergency rollback) is idempotent and prioritized over canary progression. Quench will route back to the most recent stable pinned model and trigger a canary incident with attached telemetry snapshot
We will instrument a 'dry-run' simulation mode that applies the policy to historical traces and reports projected outcomes without changing live routing
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (API/DSL): design and implement schema extensions, schema migration plan, add unit tests for parser/validator (2w)

Phase 2 (Runtime Enforcer): implement an admission/enforcement middleware in the routing layer that evaluates policy and annotates requests with lane metadata. Add fast-path for precomputed static splits. (3w)
Phase 3 (Guardrails & Quench): implement guardrail evaluation engine backed by time-windowed aggregations and circuit-breaker actions. Hook into model routing to perform rollback. (3w)
Phase 4 (Simulation + CI): build simulation harness, integrate with recorded traces (kafka archived), add smoke tests and integration tests. (2w)
Phase 5 (Console + Observability): Console UI updates for policy authoring and live step view; telemetry dashboards and alert rules. (2w)
test_plan: Unit tests for DSL parsing, validation, and guardrail predicate compilation
Load test the enforcer to ensure added latency < 50ms median; p95 impact measured in staging
Integration tests that run full canary scenarios in staging cluster using synthetic traffic harness
Chaos test: inject intermittent service errors during a canary to validate pause vs quench thresholds behave correctly
Regression tests for rollback idempotency and no-network-split condition where rollback must not leave traffic stranded
telemetry_requirements: New metrics: rollout_step_active{route,policy,step}, lane_traffic_ratio{lane,route}, guardrail_eval{guardrail,route,window}, quench_trigger_count{policy}
Tag traces with policy_id and step_id for trace correlation and fast search in Console
Capture a telemetry snapshot (5m window of key metrics + sample requests) at time of quench for postmortem
Alert rule templates for warn/critical severities that map to PagerDuty and Console notifications
rollout_strategy: We will roll the enforcer as a staged rollout itself: start with a passive dry-run on 10% of routes for 48h, then enable enforcement for low-throughput customers, followed by company-wide ramp. For Private deployments we will ship as opt-in config with migration instructions.
